amendment_metadata.purpose: Corrects artifacts/v2/phase4_baseline_results.json's ClinicalTrials metrics for the dev+validation split now that the filter.phase API defect (docs/v2/CLINICALTRIALS_PHASE_FILTER_DEFECT_FIX.md) is fixed. This is an ADDITIVE amendment layer, not an overwrite -- artifacts/v2/phase4_baseline_results.json and docs/v2/PHASE4_BASELINE_MEASUREMENT.md are left untouched except for a dated AMENDMENT section appended to the latter, matching Phase 3's config_version_history precedent for corrections.
amendment_metadata.fix_location: tools/clinical_trials_tool.py search_trials() -- filter.phase query param (HTTP 400) replaced with AREA[Phase]<value> query.term (per the standing AREA[...] pattern for condition/intervention/sponsor/country)
amendment_metadata.methodology: Same required-trial-recall and structured-filter-correctness metrics/definitions as the original baseline measurement (docs/v2/PHASE4_GATE_PLAN.md Section 1 taxonomy). Only the 3 dev+validation ClinicalTrials cases originally affected by the filter.phase defect were re-run -- not the full 49-case benchmark. Reran using the exact same params_used (condition/intervention/status/phase) recorded in the original per-case results, against the now-fixed ClinicalTrialsTool().search_trials(), max_results=20 (matching the original harness's observed 20-item cap on non-erroring cases), live against clinicaltrials.gov. compiled_filter_correctness verdicts are reproduced verbatim from the original per-case records because params_used is byte-identical before and after this fix (the fix only changed how the phase value is transmitted to the API, not what search_trials() is called with) -- that judgment could not have changed.
amendment_metadata.identification_method: Filtered artifacts/v2/phase4_baseline_results.json's per_case_results (19 dev+validation ClinicalTrials cases) for entries with a non-null `phase` in clinical_trials.params_used AND a non-null clinical_trials.error field. Exactly 3 matched -- the same 3 named in docs/v2/PHASE4_BASELINE_MEASUREMENT.md Section 3. All 5 multi_source (MS-*) cases sharing a phase-affected case family (MS-05, MS-06) were also checked directly: both compiled phase=null in their own clinical_trials.params_used (their harness path did not pass a phase filter through), so neither was affected by this defect and neither is included here.

aggregate_metrics_corrected.scope: same 19 dev+validation ClinicalTrials cases with gold as the original baseline measurement (artifacts/v2/phase4_baseline_results.json aggregate_metrics)

clinical_trials_required_trial_recall.delta: +3 cases (+0.1579), all 3 previously-erroring phase-filtered cases now hit their gold NCT ID

clinical_trials_structured_filter_correc.original_broken_tool: 0.85 (16/19 checked filter instances, per original measurement's methodology)
clinical_trials_structured_filter_correc.note: This metric judges whether the COMPILED param matched the case's stated filter, not whether the live API call succeeded. The 3 affected cases' params_used are byte-identical before and after the fix (only the transmission of phase to the API changed), so their compiled_filter_correctness verdicts (phase:true/intervention:true/condition:false for CT-MULTI-01, etc. -- see affected_cases above) are unchanged by this fix. The defect was purely an execution-layer bug (wrong API parameter causing a hard 400), not a query-compilation bug -- filter correctness was already being measured correctly at baseline.

remaining_gap_after_fix.note: CT-COND-01 (broad condition-only query, gold trial ranked beyond the returned window) and MS-06 (multi-source upadacitinib/Crohn's case, params_used had condition='Crohn's disease' rather than the rheumatoid-arthritis+phase filter combination that made CT-MULTI-02 pass) were NOT affected by the filter.phase defect -- both called search_trials() with phase=null originally and still do. Their misses are genuine ranking/query-formulation gaps unrelated to this fix and are correctly left as-is; not in scope for this amendment.
